summary: Tested new 'Refresh Drawings/ECNs' on-demand SAP attachment refresh feature (both backend endpoint and BOM Explorer UI). Backend endpoint logic is correct (empty list short-circuits, single known id returns checked/found/failed quickly, 401 without session). UI button placement/disabled-state/spinner/regression checks (ECN badge+drawing icon, mobile toolbar, Export to Excel, Load Standard Costs sanity click) all pass. However, found a reproducible CRITICAL issue: for the full 109-component BOM 5989828, the frontend's single blocking POST /api/bom/refresh-attachments call is killed by a ~60s edge/gateway (Cloudflare) timeout before the backend finishes (backend itself needs ~60-105s and DOES complete and return 200 OK server-side, data is correctly persisted to MongoDB), so the user sees a false 'Failed to refresh attachments' error toast instead of the expected success toast, even though the refresh actually succeeded. Reproduced twice (once before, once after a backend restart), confirmed via backend access logs (200 OK server-side) and by directly reading the persisted component_master doc in Mongo (correct drawing_url + ECR comment) despite the client-visible 502.

critical.issue: For BOMs with ~100+ components, the single synchronous request takes 60-105s+ which exceeds this environment's ~60s edge/proxy (Cloudflare) timeout. The backend itself completes successfully (confirmed 200 OK in backend access logs, and correct data persisted in MongoDB), but the browser/client receives a 502 'invalid or incomplete response' from Cloudflare and the frontend shows a false failure toast to the user. This defeats the button's purpose for exactly the large-BOM use case it was built for (the reviewer's own 109-part BOM 5989828 test case).

integration_issues.flow: Refresh Drawings/ECNs on a 100+ component BOM
integration_issues.issue: Toast shows 'Failed to refresh attachments' / 'origin web server returned an invalid or incomplete response to Cloudflare' instead of the expected success toast, because the single long-running POST exceeds the platform's edge timeout (~60s) even though the backend job actually finishes and persists correct data. Button UI itself recovers gracefully (returns to normal enabled state, no infinite spinner) but the user-facing message is misleading (looks like a total failure when data was actually refreshed).

action_items: Fix the edge-timeout mismatch for POST /api/bom/refresh-attachments on large BOMs: either (a) make the endpoint return immediately (202-style) and have the frontend poll a status endpoint / rely on background completion + a follow-up loadDrawingUrls() poll, or (b) chunk the product_ids client-side into smaller batches (e.g. 20-30 at a time) with sequential POSTs so each individual request stays well under the ~60s edge timeout, or (c) confirm with platform infra if the ingress/Cloudflare timeout for this route can be raised similarly to how 'Load Standard Costs' apparently handles long SAP calls (it wasn't observed to 502 in this same session, worth checking whether it uses chunked polling already and mirroring that pattern here).

Consider only showing the failure toast when the backend genuinely returns a non-2xx/timeout status distinguishable from a client-side network/gateway abort, so a 502 (proxy-level) vs a real backend error aren't both reported the same way to the user.
critical_code_review_comments: bom_categorizer.refresh_attachments_now and the /api/bom/refresh-attachments endpoint are otherwise well-written (dedupe ids, cap at 400, ThreadPoolExecutor with bounded workers, graceful per-item failure handling) - the only real defect found is architectural: a single-request/single-response design for a call whose own docstring says it can take 60-120s+ is fundamentally incompatible with typical edge/reverse-proxy default timeouts (~60s), which this preview environment's Cloudflare layer enforces.
Empty-list short circuit and MAX_IDS cap are correctly implemented and tested.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (all UI/regression checks pass; the one integration issue above affects the primary large-BOM use case)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Core backend logic (refresh_attachments_now, /api/bom/refresh-attachments) is correct and unit/integration-tested (see test_refresh_attachments.py). Frontend button, states, toolbar placement, mobile layout, and the ECN/drawing-icon regression check all pass. The one real bug is an infra/architecture mismatch: this preview env's edge proxy (Cloudflare) times out client-facing HTTP requests at ~60s, but a 109-part BOM refresh legitimately takes 60-105s+ server-side (it DOES finish correctly - verified via backend logs returning 200 and via direct MongoDB read of the refreshed component_master doc), so the browser gets a 502 and the UI shows a false failure toast. Reproduced consistently twice, including after a supervisorctl restart backend (which did NOT fix it, ruling out the stuck-thread issue mentioned in the review request's context note - this is a different, timeout-architecture issue, not stuck threads). Recommend chunking product_ids into smaller batches client-side (multiple sequential POSTs) as the most direct fix without needing infra-level timeout changes.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: /api/bom/refresh-attachments is a single long-running synchronous-style HTTP request/response (frontend awaits one POST for the entire batch). For the 109-component BOM 5989828, SAP's response time (throttled to 4 workers, further capped by a 3-concurrent sap_semaphore) makes the total call duration 60-105s+. This preview environment's edge layer (Cloudflare in front of the Kubernetes ingress) appears to enforce a client-visible response timeout of ~60s regardless of backend health, returning its own 502 to the browser once that threshold is crossed - while the backend request itself keeps running to completion and returns 200 OK server-side (visible in backend access logs) with correctly persisted data (verified in MongoDB). Reproduction steps: load BOM 5989828 (109 parts) in BOM Explorer, click 'Refresh Drawings/ECNs', wait ~60s - browser console shows a 502 and the sonner toast reads 'Failed to refresh attachments' / Cloudflare 'invalid or incomplete response', while the backend log for the same request shows 200 OK and MongoDB reflects the correct refreshed drawing_url/comments.
